sentences.text: The appellants are the land losers, who are before this Court assailing judgment dated 20.07.2021 passed by the Karnataka High SLP(C) No(s).

Court, Dharwad Bench in M.F.A. No. 100246/2021(LAC) connected with M.F.A. No.
100245/2021(LAC), M.F.A. Crob. No. 100027/2021 (LAC) & M.F.A. Crob. No. 100028/2021 (LAC)
and also the cross objections.

Though detailed consideration has been made by the High Court with reference to Section 20(ii)(c) of the Land Acquisition Amendment Act, (Karnataka Amendment) and to the decision for which the High Court of Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (KIADB), Bangalore versus Byregowda & Another (2019) 1 KLJ 805 to ultimately arrive at the conclusion that the matter is required to be remanded to the reference court.

entities.text: High Court of Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (KIADB), Bangalore versus Byregowda & Another (2019) 1 KLJ 805
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The reason for which the High Court has done so is because it was of the opinion that at the first instance the necessary parties to be arrayed in a reference proceeding under Section 18 of the Act was not appropriately arrayed.

In this regard what is to be noted is that the acquisition process was initiated by the government for the benefit of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board(KIADB) in turn allot the land to the appropriate industrial concerns.
In the instant case, the allotment of the land was made in favour of M/s Hospet Power Company (Respondent No. 1).

In this regard, it is to be noted that before the Reference Court though only the Special Land Acquisition Officer of KIADB was impleaded and neither the government nor the CEO of the KIADB was impleaded, M/s Hospet Power Company which is the ultimate beneficiary of the acquisition, who is required to pay the compensation had been impleaded.

If that SLP(C) No(s). 12650/2021 ETC.
be the position, when in the instant facts before the High Court the Chief Executive Officer and Member Secretary, KIADB was also arrayed as party.
The parties were well represented.

The evidence available before the Reference Court in any event could have been taken into consideration by the High Court to arrive at the conclusion as to whether the compensation arrived at by the Reference Court was justified or not on its merit.

Needless to mention that in the said process if the High Court was of the opinion that the matters are required to be referred back to the Reference Court for tendering evidence or for such other consideration, only in such case a remand was necessitated and not for the purpose for which it has done.

Therefore we are of the opinion that the matters require to be remanded to the High Court to consider the evidence available on record for re-appreciation of the same and to arrive at the just and fair compensation in respect of the acquired land.
In that regard all contentions of the parties are left open to be urged before the High Court.
In that view the judgment dated 20.07.2021 is set aside.

M.F.A. No. 100246/2021(LAC) connected with M.F.A. No. 100245/2021(LAC), M.F.A. Crob. No. 100027/2021 (LAC) & M.F.A. Crob. No.
100028/2021 (LAC) are restored to the file of the High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench.
